purpose: Make sound, smell, touch, light, objects, equipment, temperature, animals, and room-interruption first-class evidence without turning vividness into voyeurism or advice.
governing_sentence: The room is not background; the room is part of what was witnessed.

clusters.name: breath, machines, voice, music, interruption, silence
odor, wound, urine, breath, dignity, shame
touch, temperature, mouth, linens, body weight, body preparation
chairs, tables, phones, windows, light, equipment, removal
pets, child sensory memory, grief triggers and continuing bonds
clusters.review_gate: high gate for children; pet nonprophecy; grief boundary

hard_rules: Do not publish sensory details because they are vivid; publish only when they orient, console, contextualize, or protect.
Do not make smell, sound, touch, pets, music, or equipment into proofs, predictions, diagnoses, rituals, or advice.
Messy rooms and beautiful rooms must both be held without ranking the death.
Private objects, photographs, medicines, documents, religious items, jewelry, and room layouts may identify people and require consent review.
open_questions: Which sensory channels are most underdocumented in professional literature and best recovered through consented testimony?
How can public pages name smell and body work without humiliating the dead or the witnesses?
What should be the minimum dignity review before any sensory record graduates from quarantine?
